text: Reasoning is also generated text. A model that confabulated the conclusion will happily confabulate a convincing explanation for it. That's not a rare failure. It's the default. Any system graded only by its own output will always look consistent. Because consistency is all it was ever asked to produce. The system runs. That was never proof that it's right. The cheapest version of this is to ask the same model the same question twice and see if the answers match. That's self-consistency sampling. Its own documentation is blunt. Two identical confabulations are still confabulations. High consistency is weak positive evidence. Low consistency is strong negative evidence.
